newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges, cargoes steady, little Russian seEN.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges, cargoes steady, little Russian seEN.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges were steady in a quiet early market on Tuesday that seemed to mimic a day earlier, while cargoes were steady with little Russian material on offer, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded twice in Antwerp at $84.50 a tonne fob and once at $84.75 fob for 1,000 tonnes in Rotterdam, in the top end of Monday's range. Earlier in Rotterdam buyers were at $83/$84 and sellers at $84.50/$85.
"I think they are trying to keep prices where they are, but I won't be surprised if prices moved down to $84 this afternoon. I can already get RMG material for $84," one trader said.
On Monday, one early trade at $85 failed to set higher trading levels and the market then moved to trade as low as $83.25 by the end of the day, with low demand sapping the market.
Bunkers traded at $86/$87 a tonne delivered on board for 380 CST fuel in Antwerp while Rotterdam prices were 50 cents to $1.50 lower, traders said.
"There was a lot of ship enquiries, we closed a lot of bunkers, especially in Antwerp," one trader said.
Low sulphur barges were unchanged, with sellers standing their ground at $97 a tonne while buyers were some $2 lower.
High sulphur cargoes were steady with traders saying most of the Russian material in northern Europe has already been placed and with little on offer. Swaps were talking $83.75/$84.25 for July.

There was unconfirmed talk of an M-100 straight-run sold at two means plus $2 early in the day. Two more cargoes were heard on offer, with bids at $1.25/$1.50 over two means and offers at two means +$2 or a little more.

Traders said the market would remain stable at about the $81/$82 cif mark until Russian stuff starts appearing in bulk again in the second half of July, but the movement of crude would also be a major factor affecting its course.
